title: Block C close: the wound and the healing
hookLine: a split remembered with grief, and a family everyone loves

lines: IT BEGAN ON THE DAY AFTER.
A POOL, A CALENDAR, A FIELD, A RIVER.
cards: It began on the day after. The Prophet ﷺ had died, his body was not yet buried, and the community had to decide who would lead. Then came a pledge in a meeting hall.
A pool called Ghadir Khumm. A calendar, a Coptic boy's case, a plague. A caliph killed at home, a battle around a camel, a field called Siffin.
Hasan's peace, Husayn's refusal, a river cut off, Zaynab's voice. It's a hard stretch of history, and it has been told two ways. Today the block closes.
Today: the wound and the healing.

teach.b: Start with the wound. The question of who should lead after the Prophet was answered one way by those who pledged to Abu Bakr, and another way by those who held that the Prophet had named Ali.
Out of those answers came the Sunni telling and the Shia telling, and both carried their grief: Uthman killed while reading the Qur'an, Ali struck in the mosque at Kufa, Husayn at Karbala.
Neither tradition hides the wound. It is remembered, in sermons and in majalis. Now the healing, which was there all along.
The same family is loved on both sides; the blessing on Muhammad and his family is said in prayer by both. The four caliphs and the twelve Imams have one man in common, Ali.

teach.h: THE HEALING: ONE FAMILY, ONE QIBLAH.
teach.b: The qiblah doesn't move for anyone. And the Qur'an gives words for people who come after an earlier generation.

teach.h: FORGIVE US AND THOSE BEFORE US.
teach.b: After praising the emigrants and the helpers of Medina, it describes believers who came later and say: "Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe."
That prayer doesn't settle who was right. It asks forgiveness for everyone before us, and a heart without rancor toward everyone now. Read this way, unity isn't an agreement reached.
It's something asked for, again and again.
Unity is a prayer. Next, the path leaves the split behind and walks into the cities the Muslims built.

how: Sunni and Shia Muslims remember the early conflicts in different ways, in sermons, histories and Muharram gatherings, and the Qur'an's prayer for 'our brethren who were before us in the faith' (59:10) is recited as a prayer against rancor.

o: rancor, a grudge held in the heart
a pledge of loyalty to a new leader
a deep wound left by a battle

p: the pool in the Shia telling
forgive us and those before us

s: the early split is hidden and never spoken of in either tradition
it is remembered openly, in sermons and in Muharram gatherings.
the Qur'an's prayer in 59:10 asks forgiveness for believers who came before
forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith.
Ali appears among both the four caliphs and the twelve Imams
he is fourth of the four in Sunni reckoning and the first Imam for Twelver Shia.

games.q: you inherit an old quarrel between two sides of your community. the Qur'an's prayer in 59:10 is open in front of you. what does it ask for?
o: a ruling on which side was right.
forgiveness for those before, and no rancor toward those who believe.
that the other side be proven wrong.
games.why: the verse doesn't settle the old question; it asks forgiveness for the earlier generation and a heart free of rancor now.

practice: If you pray, say the Qur'an's words slowly: Our Lord, forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe.
If you don't, bring to mind one rift you know, in a family, a friendship or a community, and hold both sides of it without choosing, breathing in for those who came before and out for those here now.

wordCard.voice: Ghill, rancor, a grudge in the heart: the word the Qur'an's prayer asks God to remove, closing this block on the wound of the first split and the healing held in common. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: rancor, a grudge in the heart; the word in 59:10 that the prayer asks God to remove.
